newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil start talks with industry on export aid.
newsitem.headline: Brazil start talks with industry on export aid.

text.p: The Brazilian government Monday began talks with industry representatives on how best to help 15 selected sectors boost exports and narrow the country's widening trade gap, officials said.

The officials, requesting anonymity, said Ministry of Industry and Commerce technicians met in the morning with executives from the metals industry and would hold talks with car industry representatives in the afternoon.
The talks are expected to continue all week.
The meetings follow a ministry report recommending special attention be paid to 15 industrial sectors and their exports.

Apart from metals and car parts, they include capital goods, electronics, textiles, leather and shoes, chemicals, marine construction, furniture, paper and pulp, agricultural machinery, information technology, toys, fishing and civil construction.
Earlier this month, Antonio Sergio Martins de Mello, the ministry's secretary of industrial policy at the ministry, told Reuters that the idea was to boost competitiveness.
Measures being considered to raise exports include special credit lines, tax exemptions and steps to reduce the costs of doing business in Brazil, the so-called "Brazil Cost".

Brasilia has already taken some steps to help exports -- freeing raw materials and some semi-manufactured goods from export tax, reviving an export insurance agency and setting up some special credit lines.
Brazil posted a record trade deficit in 1996 of $5.539 billion. Exports grew only 2.67 percent while imports jumped 6.88 percent over 1995.
